options.text: They are too small to react
They have full outer electron shells, making them very stable
They are always kept in sealed containers

questions.explanation: Noble gases have full outer electron shells (8 electrons, or 2 for helium). This is a very stable arrangement, so they do not need to lose, gain, or share electrons. Since chemical reactions involve electron transfer or sharing, noble gases do not react.

questions.stem: Why is argon used to fill light bulbs?

options.text: It makes the bulb glow brighter
It is unreactive, so it will not react with the hot metal filament
It is cheaper than using a vacuum

questions.explanation: Argon is used in light bulbs because it is unreactive (inert). If air were used, the oxygen would react with the hot metal filament, causing it to burn out quickly. Argon prevents oxidation, extending the filament's life. Argon is also cheap as it makes up about 1% of air.
